name: thread-m8-3-turns
why: Three turns of ISO M8 x 1.25, right- and left-handed, as two bodies. Closed form, derived in the script from the ISO 68-1 basic profile (core at the basic minor radius 3.323418, tooth 3P/4 wide there and P/8 at r = 4): a horizontal slice of a screw-symmetric solid has one area at every height, so V = pi r1^2 L + 2 pi L / P * integral r w(r) dr = 155.098715 mm3 per body at L = 3.75, for either hand. The exact B-rep reads it within 3e-6 (BRepGProp on a STEP round trip), and the kernel refuses any thread whose built volume is more than 2e-5 from this form, so that check runs on every build; the volumes recorded here are the meshes', about 0.15% under the solid because a 0.68 mm tooth's facets at 0.01 mm deflection cut its curved flanks. Before the construction was chosen, the same rod built with a core shorter than the swept tooth, or squared by a common with a cylinder, came back valid, closed and 16-100% short; the topology recorded here is the construction that measured right (docs/GOTCHAS.md, 'Threads').
